barriers.description: The project lacked budget to procure devices, forcing the team to rely only on existing user devices during design and testing.
barriers.justification: This financial constraint limited the team's ability to specify device requirements, produce and evaluate prototypes across consistent hardware, and plan realistic deployment scenarios.
barriers.reference_excerpt: It should be noted this project did not include funds for pro- curement of devices so only existing devices could be used.

barriers.description: Poor network connectivity and sporadic electricity in the field constrained what digital functionality could be designed and tested.
barriers.justification: Unreliable connectivity and power impeded the team's ability to evaluate digital designs in realistic conditions and required them to change design requirements (e.g., include paper-based tools), limiting iterative digital testing.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Network connectivity was poor, and electricity to charge phones was sporadic.

barriers.description: County governments lacked budgetary capacity to maintain separate software, forcing designers to constrain solutions to be sustainable without county-funded maintenance.
barriers.justification: This external funding and capacity limitation constrained specification of system requirements and design options (e.g., must work on personal phones, include paper backups), thus narrowing feasible prototypes and evaluation scenarios.
barriers.reference_excerpt: For the system to be sustainable, it had to be applicable for all CHVs across Kenya; these counties alone do not have the capacity or budget to maintain the software. CHVs would need to use personal phones as procuring devices was not possible; county budgets are limited and maintaining broken or lost devices over the long term was not feasible.

barriers.description: HCD requires specialized expertise that individuals working in government settings may not possess, making internal adoption and local leadership of the process difficult.
barriers.justification: Limited HCD knowledge among government stakeholders hindered the designers' ability to transfer methods, build local capacity, and coordinate multidisciplinary teams for sustained HCD activities and iterative implementation.
barriers.reference_excerpt: It should be noted that HCD requires specialized expertise to lead the process, and individuals working in governments of low- and middle-income coun- tries may not have these skills. At this time, HCD is a specialized methodology that requires external as- sistance.

barriers.description: The HCD process required substantial up-front time and resources (7 months), which exceeded typical timelines for program design.
barriers.justification: The long lead time constrained rapid iteration and increased resource demands on the design team, affecting their ability to integrate feedback quickly and potentially delaying evaluation and implementation activities.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Compared to other pro- gram design approaches, HCD and systems analysis can take a greater time investment up front (in this case it took 7 months). The approach requires significant time before implementation to conduct the research (2 to 3 months), thoroughly under- stand the end users (and establish trust with them), and develop and repeatedly test the design and high-fidelity prototypes of the solutions (2 to 3 months).
